plan Grand River Dam Authority.pages: GRDA publishes no resource plan document. Its planning is in board minutes. Read in full: the special meeting minutes of September 29, 2025 (5 pages, https://grda.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/09292025-Approved-Minutes-Special-Meeting.pdf), where page 2 to 3 cover the Southwest Power Pool expedited study and the planning options, and the special meeting minutes of October 9, 2025 (5 pages, https://grda.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/10092025-Special-Board-Meeting-Approved-Minutes.pdf), where page 2 covers Glencoe and the Lenapah site. Also read the April 8, 2026 board agenda and request for quotes 2871 for Glencoe. Also read: the approved minutes of October, November and December 2025 and January 2026, and every agenda from October 2025 to October 2026. The January 14, 2026 minutes, item 9, page 5, put Unit 4 at 96.3 percent complete with first fire in February 2026. The April 8, 2026 agenda (https://grda.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/FINAL-AGENDA-FOR-04-08-2026-Mtg.pdf), page 3, Fuel and Long-Range Planning Committee item 2, is Phase II of the Southwest Power Pool study for the Glencoe Energy Center. The August 12, 2026 agenda (https://grda.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/FINAL-AGENDA-08122026-Board-Meeting-2.pdf), page 4, item 1 of the same committee, is a combustion turbine reservation agreement. A NonDoc article of February 17, 2025 on the bond bill was read in full.

additions.what: Glencoe Energy Center in Payne County: October 9, 2025 minutes page 2 give an engineering update with a Southwest Power Pool interconnection application, layout drawings, soil studies and a schedule. No fuel or size is stated.

Grand River Energy Center Unit 4, a new 426 MW gas simple cycle turbine. The January 14, 2026 minutes, item 9, page 5, say 96.3 percent complete with first fire targeted for February 6 to 20, 2026. GEM lists it as operating, 2026.

options.what: Upgrade of Grand River Energy Center Unit 4 to a combined cycle, using the former Unit 1 grid connection (September 29, 2025 minutes page 3). The same page compares a Unit 4 steam turbine upgrade in two scenarios.
Life extension of coal Unit 2 at Grand River Energy Center through the Southwest Power Pool expedited study, about $70 million (September 29, 2025 minutes pages 2 to 3).
100-hour battery storage and a compressed air storage project for Google (September 29, 2025 minutes page 3).
options.why_not: Storage, not a gas or oil unit, and no site is named for the batteries.

options.what: A site near Lenapah in Nowata County with an option agreement and a water permit application (October 9, 2025 minutes page 2).
options.why_not: The minutes name no fuel, size or type of plant for the Lenapah site, and no Southwest Power Pool request or air permit names it yet.

options.what: House Bill 1422 raised GRDA's bond limit to pay for a 450 MW simple cycle gas unit, a 640 MW combined cycle gas unit, a refit of the Salina pumped storage plant and the retirement of a 492 MW coal unit (NonDoc, February 17, 2025, https://nondoc.com/2025/02/17/grda-bond-capacity-requrest-generating-controversy/). No site is given for the combined cycle.
options.note: The 450 MW unit is Unit 4. The combined cycle matches the Unit 4 combined cycle upgrade in the September 29, 2025 minutes, page 3, already listed here.

options.what: A combustion turbine reservation agreement before the Fuel and Long-Range Planning Committee (August 12, 2026 agenda, page 4, item 1).
options.why_not: The agenda gives no size, site or unit count, and the minutes for that meeting are not posted yet. It may belong to Glencoe, which is on the watch list.

plan Grand River Dam Authority.evidence: September 29, 2025 minutes page 3: GRDA is limited in its gas supply at the Grand River Energy Center, so anything added there would have to be something other than natural gas; upgrading Unit 4 adds no strain on gas supply. October 9, 2025 minutes page 2: engineering update on the planned Glencoe Energy Center in Payne County, and the Lenapah property in Nowata County is still available with an option agreement and a water permit application. Glencoe is staged as a watch item because no source gives its fuel or size.
plan Grand River Dam Authority.read_by_hand: GRDA minutes from February 2026 on are not posted, so only the agendas were read for those months. The November 2026 agenda is not posted. GRDA bond papers on EMMA, the municipal bond disclosure site, need its search form and were not read. A person should open the minutes for August 12, 2026 when posted to see what the turbine reservation is for.
plan Grand River Dam Authority.newer_checked: GRDA has never published a resource plan. Agendas through October 2026 were read on November 6, 2026 for any newer planning item; the newest are the Glencoe study and the turbine reservation.

plan Oklahoma Municipal Power Authority.pages: OMPA publishes no plan document. Its planning is in its board minutes (index https://www.ompa.com/board-of-directors-minutes/). Read in full: the 15 sets of minutes from July 2024 to September 2025. Lamb is on August 8, 2024 page 5 item 13 (request of about 103 MW), September 2024 pages 4 to 5 item 8 (Sargent and Lundy study of two smaller units at Lamb), October 2024 page 6 (124 MW, two Siemens units), December 2024 page 6 (about $70 million for the new Lamb unit before service in 2029), April 2025 retreat page 6 (stay in the study at 124 MW and ask for bids), June 2025 page 4 item 13 (Southern Star gas transport of 24,000 dekatherms a day for the new Lamb unit), August 2025 page 4 (Resolution 2025-8-C, Lamb capacity upgrade) and September 2025 page 4 item 12 (one turbine bid, delivery not until 2029). July 2024 page 4 has Redbud and page 5 McClain.

additions.what: New gas turbine at the Charles D. Lamb plant in Kay County. Planned as two Siemens units at 124 MW in the October 2024 and April 2025 minutes, then one GE 7E.03 of 90 MW in the May 2026 air permit application. Southwest Power Pool request GEN-2024-334, 103 MW, service June 1, 2029.
Redbud upgrade, about 23 MW for OMPA in 2027 (minutes page 4).
New turbines at the McClain site, which OMPA co-owns with OG&E at 23 percent of the land; OMPA approved a site control letter so OG&E can file its interconnection request (minutes page 5).

options.what: In July 2024 OMPA was studying another generator with Sargent and Lundy (minutes page 5).
options.note: The September 2024 minutes name the study's site as Lamb, so this is the new Lamb unit.

plan Oklahoma Municipal Power Authority.evidence: OMPA's planning since July 2024 settles on one new gas turbine at Lamb, the Redbud upgrade and the McClain turbines. The Lamb unit is staged as Lamb Unit 2 and is Southwest Power Pool request GEN-2024-334. July 8, 2024 minutes page 4: OMPA expects a shortage of about 30 MW in 2026 and counts an estimated 72 MW from a solar plant and 23 MW from the Redbud upgrade in 2027. Page 5: OG&E is looking to add turbines at the McClain site, and OMPA is investigating adding a generator. Both are tied to plants or records already in this batch or in GEM.

plan Western Farmers Electric Cooperativ.pages: Western Farmers keeps an internal resource plan, updated each year, that is not public. Read instead: the federal Rural Utilities Service environmental assessment for new generation at Hugo (https://www.rd.usda.gov/media/file/download/rus-ea-hugo-new-generation.pdf, 136 pages), whose purpose and need and alternatives sections describe the July 8, 2025 plan; the draft assessment for the Anadarko turbines (https://www.rd.usda.gov/media/file/download/usda-rd-anadarko-power-plant-combustion-turbine-draft-ea.pdf, 99 pages), section 1.2.3 and the project description, with the fleet table; and the 2024 and 2025 annual reports (2025: https://www.wfec.com/s/2026-Ann-Report_2026-04-20.pdf, page 6 on Hugo and Anadarko).

additions.what: Nine new simple cycle gas turbines at the Hugo plant in Choctaw County, 404 MW in the 2025 annual report page 6 and 415.5 MW in the Hugo assessment section 1, service in 2029, gas pipeline in the third quarter of 2028. GEM lists Hugo Site A and Site B, 415.5 MW together, pre-construction, 2029.

Two GE LM6000 gas turbines, Roulet 12 and 13, 50.2 MW each, at the Anadarko plant in Caddo County, completion September 2026, replacing gas boilers 1R, 2R and 3 (Anadarko draft assessment section 1.2.3; 2025 annual report page 6). GEM lists Roulet 12 and 13 under construction, 2026, and unit 3 retired.

options.what: The assessments compare batteries, a small modular reactor and gas turbines before choosing gas turbines (Hugo assessment alternatives section).
options.why_not: The batteries and the reactor were rejected, and neither is a gas or oil unit.

options.what: Mooreland plant, three gas steam units of 329 MW (Anadarko draft assessment fleet table).
options.why_not: No new unit or retirement date is given for Mooreland in any document read, so there is nothing to change.

plan Western Farmers Electric Cooperativ.evidence: Western Farmers' plan, as described in the two Rural Utilities Service assessments, finds a capacity deficit and chooses gas turbines at Hugo and Anadarko. Both projects are already in GEM with matching size, status and year. No regulator filing of the plan exists; the Oklahoma commission's plan rule covers only utilities it regulates.
plan Western Farmers Electric Cooperativ.read_by_hand: The plan itself is not public and no regulator holds it. The Hugo assessment was read for its plan sections only, not all 136 pages. The Western Area Power Administration plan list (https://apps.wapa.gov/IRP/IRPMain) gave no response, and Western Farmers is not known as one of its customers. Bond papers on EMMA were not read.
plan Western Farmers Electric Cooperativ.newer_checked: The Hugo assessment cites the July 8, 2025 plan, the newest version found. The 2025 annual report of April 20, 2026 has the latest project news. A person could ask Western Farmers for the 2026 update.
plan Western Farmers Electric Cooperativ.names_checked: Hugo Power Plant is GEM's Hugo power station, L100000104123. Orme Plant and the Genco units are 45 MW turbines at Anadarko, each under the 50 MW per unit threshold, so they are correctly absent from GEM. LCEC Generation Plant is in Lovington, New Mexico, at 42 MW in all, outside Oklahoma and under the threshold.

plan Associated Electric Cooperative Inc.pages: Associated Electric's 2022 resource plan is not public. Read instead: the federal Rural Utilities Service final environmental assessment for the Ripley Energy Center (https://www.rd.usda.gov/media/file/download/usda-rd-ea-ripley-energy-center-09102024.pdf), the introduction, purpose and need, and alternatives sections, pages 1-1 to 1-6 and section 2.1; and the cooperative's pages on new gas generation (https://www.aeci.org/new-gas-generation), Bristow (https://www.aeci.org/bristow-energy-center-1, Fast Facts) and Ripley (https://www.aeci.org/ripleyenergycenter).

additions.what: Ripley Energy Center, one simple cycle gas turbine of 421 MW, 6.5 miles north of Ripley in Payne County (Ripley assessment pages 1-1 and 1-6). GEM lists 445 MW under construction, 2027.

Bristow Energy Center, a gas peaking turbine of 420 MW net, 2 miles southeast of Bristow in Creek County, construction from 2027 over about two years (Bristow page, Fast Facts). GEM lists 420 MW, pre-construction, 2029.
Chouteau combined cycle plant in Mayes County: no new unit or retirement in any document read.

options.what: The 2022 plan found a need of 844 MW by winter 2027 and chose up to 900 MW of new gas across Missouri and Oklahoma after a request for proposals whose best bid cost about $200 million more than building its own (Ripley assessment section 2.1).
options.why_not: The rejected bids are not named, and the chosen plants, Ripley and Bristow in Oklahoma and Turney in Missouri, are all tied here or in the Missouri batch.

plan Associated Electric Cooperative Inc.evidence: Associated Electric's 2022 plan is known through the Ripley assessment. Its Oklahoma outcome is two gas turbines of about 420 MW, at Ripley and at Bristow, both already in GEM. The Ripley size in GEM, 445 MW, differs from the assessment's 421 MW. The Ripley RP1 capacity card in this batch already proposes 419 MW, with a question on it.
plan Associated Electric Cooperative Inc.read_by_hand: The plan is not public. The Ripley assessment was read for its plan sections only, not every page. The reports page holds only audited financial statements on Issuu, which were not read. Bond papers on EMMA were not read.
plan Associated Electric Cooperative Inc.newer_checked: No newer plan than 2022 was found on aeci.org or in news on November 6, 2026. The Bristow page, live that day, is the newest project source.
